The main takeaway from our work is that
a large-deviation principle can be used to derive bounds on the minimizer in a stochastic optimization problem without any convexity assumptions on the risk function.

the minimizer can be estimated to within any given accuracy with probability approaching 1 as the number of design points approaches a certain threshold that is independent of the number of observations at each design point.
